description: I'm developing FirePulse for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. FirePulse is an interactive application that explores historical satellite hotspot activity using MODIS and VIIRS data. It focuses on sensor comparison, historical fire calendars, seasonal anomaly analysis and geospatial visualisation.
summary:
FirePulse is a satellite fire-activity exploration platform developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.”

The project addresses differences between MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations by processing, cleaning, comparing, and harmonizing satellite hotspot records. It provides an interactive dashboard with fire-activity maps, historical monthly fire calendars, trend visualizations, sensor comparisons, and seasonal anomaly analysis, with a focus on Sri Lanka and the surrounding region.

By bringing these observations together in one platform, FirePulse helps users explore historical patterns of detected thermal activity and identify unusual seasonal changes. It also provides data-quality information to help users understand the limitations of satellite observations.

FirePulse is intended as an exploratory analysis and visualization tool. A detected hotspot is not necessarily a confirmed fire event or a measure of burned area.
details:
FirePulse is an interactive web application designed to explore and analyse historical satellite active-fire observations from NASA FIRMS.

How it works

The application processes MODIS and VIIRS hotspot CSV records through a data-processing pipeline. It validates records, handles invalid or missing values, applies quality filters, and generates cleaned datasets and analytical summaries. It then compares observations from different satellite sensors and calculates a harmonized fire-activity index to support historical comparisons.

Main features

  • Interactive map for exploring satellite hotspot locations.
  • Historical monthly fire calendar for examining seasonal patterns.
  • Trend visualizations for exploring changes in detected activity.
  • MODIS and VIIRS sensor comparison.
  • Seasonal anomaly analysis to identify unusual activity compared with historical patterns.
  • Data-quality information and downloadable analytical outputs.

Technology

The backend uses Python, including pandas and NumPy for data processing, with a lightweight Python HTTP server and API. The frontend uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Leaflet for interactive maps and Chart.js for visualizations. OpenStreetMap provides map tiles.

Intended impact

FirePulse makes historical satellite fire observations easier to explore and compare. It can support environmental research, exploratory analysis, and public understanding of seasonal fire-activity patterns, particularly in Sri Lanka and the surrounding region.

The platform is an exploratory analysis tool, not an operational fire-warning system. Satellite hotspots represent detected thermal anomalies and should not be treated as confirmed fire events, burned-area measurements, or direct measures of fire risk.

The project considers differences in sensor characteristics, data quality, observation coverage, and the limitations of comparing satellite detections across time.
